title: Word gets around
teaches: Speaking for you to someone else
blurb: A hamlet where the reeve gives her guest-stick only to strangers her neighbours speak well of.
after: What you do travels further than you do: at the well, on errands, to the people who decide. Bad news travels faster.
refines: Does news really spread in a few minutes (meetings, errands, vouching)? Do players see it travel?

things.name: guest-stick
things.description: A carved hazel stick with Oakley's mark burnt into it. Whoever carries it is the hamlet's guest.

things.name: axe head
things.description: Cob's axe head, sound and sharp, with the stub of a split handle still jammed in its eye.

things.name: ash stave
things.description: A straight, seasoned ash stave about a yard long: good handle wood.

things.name: drawknife
things.description: Cob's two-handled drawknife, for shaving wood, left on the chopping block.

things.name: fallen oak branches
things.description: Dry fallen branches under the oak: good firewood, free to anyone.

things.name: clean linen strips
things.description: Clean linen strips from Liss's loom, rolled up by her door: they'd bind a wound.

things.name: yarrow plants
things.description: Feathery yarrow growing by the path. Old wives pack wounds with it to stop the bleeding.

steps.title: Oakley
cards: …signal. A hamlet of five households. Reeve Agna keeps its guest-stick: whoever carries it is fed and housed by anyone here.
She gives it only to strangers the neighbours speak well of. People here talk: at the well, on errands, to Agna. What you do for one of them, all of them hear. What you do to one of them, too.
There's no one right way, and no words to copy. The device helps if you ask (H).

steps.title: The guest-stick
cards: Earn Agna's guest-stick. She won't give it on your word: let the hamlet's word reach her.
steps.task: Get Agna to let you carry the guest-stick
steps.done: News travelled, and Agna heard it. People here carry what you do to everyone else, good and bad.
help: Everyone here needs something: Cob's axe, Liss's hand, Old Fenn's cold hearth. Help one and they'll talk.
You can ask someone you've helped to put in a word with Agna. Or wait: they meet at the well and pass on the news.

playtest.say: That axe looks broken. Can I help?
Yes, I'll make you a new handle.

playtest.do: shave the ash stave into an axe handle with Cob's drawknife and fit the axe head on it

playtest.say: Here's your axe, with a new handle.
Good day, Reeve. I've been helping Cob. May I carry the guest-stick?
I'd be glad to help anyone else here, too. Is there anyone who needs a hand?
Thank you for hearing me out, Reeve. Oakley's a good place.

2.say: Your hand's bleeding badly. May I bind it with your linen?

2.do: bind Liss's cut hand tightly with the clean linen strips

2.say: Keep it raised. Would you tell Agna I'm no thief?

2.do: give Old Fenn the fallen oak branches for his fire

2.say: For your hearth, grandfather. It's cold for sitting out.
Good day, Reeve. Liss will tell you I helped her. May I carry the guest-stick?
I'll help anyone here who needs it. I only want a place by a fire tonight.
Thank you for hearing me out, Reeve. Oakley's a good place.

try_also: make Cob a new axe handle from the stave

reactions.killed: …You killed someone. That can't be undone. Rewind from the menu if that isn't what you meant.
reactions.arrested: They've taken you away. Rewind from the menu to try again.
reactions.dead: You died. Rewind to the last calm moment and try something else.
